answer: A sybil swarm dies by collateral lockup. To register one identity the protocol demands a bond posted from a real balance and held for a full epoch; a gale of fake accounts must each find fresh capital, so the cost of N identities grows linearly with N, never with the benefit they claim. Because voting weight, rewards and reputation derive from that same bond, spinning up its echo farms merely reshuffles the same pie. An attacker facing a hollow treasury has no cheap beacon to light: every extra key needs its own funding, and mass exit would slash or forfeit the pooled stake.
